# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure and find the labeling logic.

# 1. Overall repo structure

**Repo root:** `/app` — a single-language **Python 3.9** project (Flask REST micro-service). Git repo with one branch (`main`) and one commit (`0a1b6a3 import codebase`). No README, no CI config, no `requirements.txt`, no lint config.

```
/app
├── .gitignore
├── Dockerfile                      # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on :9898
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                    # package "categorizationapp"; deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4,
    │                               # python-Levenshtein, fuzzywuzzy, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, gunicorn
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py             # Flask app factory + request timing logging
        ├── Controller.py           # 936 lines – HTTP routes / per-bank dispatch
        ├── BankScripts/            # 35 files – one per Indian bank (bank-specific narration parsing)
        └── UtilityScripts/         # 13 files – shared enrichment logic + regex constant tables
```

Total ~11,150 lines of Python. Note: `BankScripts/` and `UtilityScripts/` have **no `__init__.py`** (implicit namespace packages), and `setup.py` lists only `packages=['categorizationapp']`, so only an editable install (`pip install -e .`, as the Dockerfile does) works reliably.

### Architecture / data flow

Everything is **vectorised pandas**: each rule is a `[boolean-Series condition, choice]` pair collected into a list `conditions_choices`, then applied with `np.select(conditions, choices, default=...)`. The columns produced/mutated are:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `description` | input narration/remark text (from `remark` too, for some banks) |
| `transactionCategory` | level-1 label (e.g. `UPI`, `NEFT`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `REVERSAL`, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`) |
| `transactionSubcategory` | level-2 label / purpose (e.g. `SALARY`, `LOAN_REPAYMENT`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`) |
| `merchantType` | sub-tag (e.g. `NBFC`, `Electricity`, `Mutual Fund`, `Fast Food`) |
| `partyName` | extracted counterparty/payee name |
| `party2` | `partyName` with spaces stripped (used for fuzzy-ish regex matching) |
| `pfmCategoryOne`/`pfmCategoryTwo`/`pfmCategoryType` | PFM taxonomy (optional) |
| `pfmSimpleDescription`, `isInternalPayment`, `city`, `Group_ID` | extras |

**Pipeline order** (see `Controller.py:91-930`, repeated verbatim per bank):
1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` → 2. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` (category + subcategory + raw `partyName` extraction) → 3. (credit cards) `card_clean_names` + `card_purpose` → 4. `purpose(...)` (subcategory + merchantType) → 5. `clean_names(...)` (payee normalisation) → 6. `internal_payment(...)` → 7. `salary_detection(...)` (SAVING only) → 8. `pfm_categorization` + `simple_description` (if `isPFMEnabled`).

**HTTP endpoints** (`Controller.py`): `GET /` (`:51`), `POST /recurrentTransactions` (`:55`), `POST /categorizeTransaction` (`:69`, the main one; bank dispatch chain `:91`–`:932`).

### How to run / tests

- **Run:** `docker build -t txn-enrich . && docker run -p 9898:9898 txn-enrich` (Dockerfile lines 1-11), or locally `cd /app/categorizationapp && pip install -e . && gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (or `python -m categorizationapp` via the `__main__` block at `__init__.py:30-31`).
- **Tests: there are NONE.** No `tests/`, no `test_*.py`/`*_test.py`, no `pytest.ini`/`tox.ini`/`setup.cfg`/`conftest.py`, no `.github/` workflows, no fixture CSV/JSON data (`*.csv` is even git-ignored — `.gitignore:52`). `git ls-files` confirms only the 54 files listed above. The only "testing" traces are commented-out dendrogram plotting blocks (`SalaryDetection.py:27-32`, `RecurrentTxns.py:16-21`) and comments like `# For testing purpose only`.

steps.message:
All five reported cases traced to four one-token defects in two bank parsers. Each was reproduced from a synthetic row first, then fixed.

## Fixes

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py`**

1. **L100 — cheque deposit read as generic transfer.** `remark.str.len().eq(15)` combined with `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` (which needs ≥16 chars) made the rule unsatisfiable, so these credits fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Changed to `.eq(16)`, matching HDFC's 16-char reference convention already used at L214-215. As the last condition in `np.select`, it can only reclaim rows that previously hit the default.

2. **L124 — salary sub-tag lost on bare numeric narration.** Guard read `accountType=="SAVINGS"`; the codebase-wide token is `SAVING` (Controller L106, ICICI L105/L113, SBI L156). Never fired. Fixed.

3. **L98 — reversal recorded as bounce.** `description.eq(description.shift(periods=2))` compared the credit's narration against the row *two* back while comparing amount/type against the *adjacent* row. The offsetting credit therefore missed `REVERSAL` and fell to the `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rule below. Changed to `shift(periods=1)`, consistent with the identical rule in ICICI L49, Saraswat L20, StandardCharted L60.

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py`**

4. **L147 — 4-field bill transfer payee.** `BIL/INFT/<numeric ref>/<name>` used `sep_by_(description,2,3)`, lifting field 2 (the numeric reference) instead of the trailing name. Changed to `(3,4)`.

5. **L159 — direction word instead of counterparty.** `py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=1)`; `py_extract` indexes capture groups positionally, so `index=0` returned `TO`/`FROM`. `"To"` was then blanked downstream by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` rule (L233) and `"From"` survived — exactly the "empty or wrong" split reported. Sibling rules already use `index=1` for leading alternation groups (ICICI L168, DCB L80-81, Kotak L233).

## Regression verification

Differential run of old vs. new over a ~4,900-row (HDFC) and ~2,000-row (ICICI) synthetic corpus spanning every rule family, across `SAVING`/`CURRENT`/`OVER_DRAFT`: **every changed row is accounted for by one of the four reported narration/remark shapes; zero unexplained changes.**

An exhaustive 512-sequence sweep for the reversal rule shows two change classes: the reported `DEBIT→CREDIT` same-narration pair now yielding `REVERSAL`, and `A(debit) B(debit) A(credit)` losing its former `REVERSAL` label — the latter being the spurious branch of the old mixed-offset predicate (narration matched 2 rows back, amount matched the adjacent row), which no other bank's copy of this rule produces.

Full pipeline (`categorize → purpose → clean_names`) runs clean on all cases.
